Island X: the default training fishery

Source: R/fishery.R
island_x.Rd

Settings for cpueTargeting::simulate_logbook() with landing sites, after Island X of the FAO training concept by Pedro Barros (Data Collection and Estimation of Fisheries Quantities): 9 landing sites of 3 types (Harbour, Beach, Jetty) and three segments (fishing-unit types) with different ranges, home tactics and site preferences:

Usage

island_x(
  boats = c(canoe = 150, small_motor = 60, large_motor = 15),
  range = c(canoe = 5, small_motor = 12, large_motor = 25),
  trips = 16000,
  n_years = 10,
  start_year = 2016,
  entry = 0.4,
  exit = 0.1
)

Arguments

boats

Number of boats per segment.

range

Fishing range per segment, in cells.

trips

Trips in an average year (all segments).

n_years

Number of years simulated.

start_year

First calendar year.

entry

Share of boats entering the fleet after year 1.

exit

Share of boats leaving the fleet before the last year.

Value

A settings list for cas_fishery().

Details

SegmentBoatsRange (cells, 2.5 km)Home tacticsBased at
canoe1505Reefbeaches, jetties
small_motor6012Reef, Sedimentall site types
large_motor1525Pelagic, Sedimentharbours, some jetties

By default 10 years are simulated: 5 years of burn-in (depletion, fleet change) and a 5-year sampling programme in the final years (see run_survey()).

Fishing pressure is moderate: catchability q = 0.004, and the reef species Dentex dentex, the most valuable and most exposed to the canoes, has its catchability by tactic reduced to 30%. Stocks decline but do not collapse (Dentex to about half of its unfished biomass by year 10).

Boats join and leave the fleet: a share entry of the boats enters after year 1 and a share exit of the others leaves, spread evenly over the years. Trips per year follow the expected number of active boats, so a growing fleet fishes more, and an old frame survey (one that counts the boats of an earlier year) misses the new boats.
